response.sql: SELECT d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS num_accounts FROM account a JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id WHERE ('19' || substr(a.date, 1, 2) || '-' || substr(a.date, 3, 2) || '-' || substr(a.date, 5, 2)) > '1994-06-17' AND ('19' || substr(a.date, 1, 2) || '-' || substr(a.date, 3, 2) || '-' || substr(a.date, 5, 2)) < '1996-09-02' GROUP BY d.A3 ORDER BY d.A3;

assumptions.assumption: account.date is stored as YYMMDD text, as documented, so it is converted to 'YYYY-MM-DD' text (century 19) before the string comparison with the stated bounds. A literal comparison of the raw value would compare '9...' against '1...' and return nothing useful.
Two-digit years are read as 19YY, which fits the dataset's 1990s dates.
The bounds are exclusive, and the join is inner, so accounts whose district_id is missing from the district table are dropped. Each account is counted once under its district's region (district.A3).

alternatives.interpretation: Compare the raw stored account.date text directly against the literal strings '1994-06-17' and '1996-09-02', with no conversion. This is the literal reading of 'compared as text', but it matches no rows when dates are stored as YYMMDD.
